subject.title: Telegram detached subagents can run silently without liveness or terminal notification

question: Should this issue stay as the canonical Telegram detached-subagent liveness and terminal-delivery contract, or should the terminal bug and liveness/status policy be split across the existing generic activity and owner-session delivery work?
rationale: The remaining work crosses Telegram transport UX, subagent announcement policy, task/session state, possible configuration, and an open partial terminal-delivery PR, so automation should not choose the permanent public delivery contract alone.

options.title: Split Terminal Bug First
options.body: Fix the raw child-output and parent-resume/terminal-delivery behavior against existing subagent announcement and task state, then decide sparse liveness and status policy as a follow-up.

options.title: Keep One Telegram Slice
options.body: Use this issue as the full Telegram-visible liveness and terminal-notification slice, coordinating with the generic activity and owner-session completion PRs as dependencies.

options.title: Fold Into Generic Activity
options.body: Move the Telegram evidence into the broader session activity and owner-session completion work, then close this only after the Telegram-specific requirements are explicitly tracked there.

recommendation.title: Split Terminal Bug First
recommendation.body: Fix the raw child-output and parent-resume/terminal-delivery behavior against existing subagent announcement and task state, then decide sparse liveness and status policy as a follow-up.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest current-main routing candidate for the subagent/task/Telegram boundary and the likely person to decide whether to split or keep the Telegram-specific contract.
